info.title: LLM Pulse API
info.description: REST API for the LLM Pulse AI visibility platform. Track brand mentions, citations, sentiment, and Share of Voice across AI-generated answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and optional add-on models). Includes the MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoint for AI clients. MCP is available on every plan and during eligible trials via OAuth 2.1, with Bearer-token API keys also accepted for headless integrations on the Scale plan or above. Full machine-readable reference at https://llmpulse.ai/api-docs/llms-full.txt. An API key can be limited to one or several projects when it is created, and the set never changes. Such a key sees only those projects: any other project id, domain or name answers ERR_PROJECT_NOT_FOUND exactly like a project that does not exist, listings return only those projects' rows, and operations on the whole account (creating or deleting a project, the project draft wizard) answer ERR_KEY_PROJECT_SCOPED. Operations carry vendor extensions: x-plan is the plan or entitlement the endpoint requires beyond an API key (growth, scale or reputation_access), x-write marks endpoints that need a read and write key, x-mcp-tool names the MCP tool that returns the same data, x-mcp-plan gives that tool's plan where it differs, and x-rest-only explains an endpoint with no MCP tool. Parameters are read strictly, on REST and MCP alike: a value outside a documented enum, a boolean other than true, false, 1 or 0, an id or count that is not a plain positive number (12abc, 1.0 or 0), an id of a record the project does not have, or a from later than to answers 422 ERR_INVALID_PARAM naming the parameter, never an ignored filter. A listed value, in a query or a request body, matches in any letter case and is read in its documented spelling (granularity=Week reads as week, aggregation_type=BYPAGE as byPage, event_type=Mention.Created as mention.created). page and per_page keep their own rule: a value that is not a number reads as absent and an out-of-range one is clamped.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Health check that validates an API key and, optionally, access to a project.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Plan, subscription window, quota consumption and API rate limits for the authenticated account. Read it before spending quota so an integration can see its remaining budget instead of discovering the ceiling by hitting it.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: A project is one tracked brand. List and read projects, see which AI models and locales have data, create a project in one call or through the multi-step draft wizard, update its profile, or delete it.

tags.name: Metrics
tags.description: Aggregated visibility, share of voice, citation and position data for the project and its competitors: time series, period summary, per-prompt summary, Share of Voice and top cited sources.

tags.name: Competitors
tags.description: The brands tracked alongside your own. Competitor ids are the actor_id values the metrics endpoints report against.

tags.name: Prompts
tags.description: The questions executed against the AI models every week, and the execution records each run produces.

tags.name: Collections & Tags
tags.description: Collections (labelled Tags in the app) group prompts by topic, funnel stage or campaign so metrics can be filtered by them.

tags.name: Answers
tags.description: The AI responses behind every metric, with their full text, mentions, citations and sentiment analysis.

tags.name: Mentions & Citations
tags.description: The raw records behind the visibility metrics: one row per brand mention or per cited URL, for the project brand, for competitors, or for both in a single stream.

tags.name: Sentiments
tags.description: Sentiment records with their comments, topics and scores, plus the category catalog used to label them.

tags.name: Sources & Citation Intelligence
tags.description: Every URL extracted from AI responses, plus grouped URL, domain and host views, page-cache metadata, mention evidence inside cited pages, occurrences and sanitized cached content.

tags.name: AI Model Insights
tags.description: Aggregate AI Model Insights report endpoints (summary, position distribution, AI Overview results). All place each answer on the day it was created (Europe/Madrid time), as the app does, and share a standard actor shape.

tags.name: AI & Agent Traffic
tags.description: What AI sends to your site: referral traffic from AI assistants measured by the connected web analytics provider, and AI crawler traffic hitting your origin server. Scale plan and above.

tags.name: Shopping & Ads
tags.description: Commercial surfaces inside AI answers: the product cards models return, the paid placements that run alongside them, and the local businesses they list for prompts with local intent. Shopping and ads need the Scale plan or above; local businesses are available on every plan.

tags.name: Owned Media & Communities
tags.description: Which of your own channels and which community conversations AI answers cite: YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, LinkedIn, app-store listings and Reddit, with each tab's summary, the answers behind one cited item, and the profiles a project claims. Growth plan and above.

tags.name: Reputation & Studies
tags.description: Multi-model analyst reports: the monthly reputation scoring of your brand against its competitors, and the custom AI studies you define over any subjects and dimensions. Requires reputation monitoring.

tags.name: Search Console
tags.description: Google Search Console performance data (impressions, clicks, CTR, average position) for projects with a connected GSC property: headline totals, time series, top queries and top pages. Growth plan and above.

tags.name: Custom Reports
tags.description: The custom reports built under Reports > Custom Reports: list them, read one with the data of every widget as its page shows it, and email it to its recipients now. Scale plan and above.

tags.name: Recommendations
tags.description: Recommendation runs that power the in-app Recommendations page, the endpoint that launches a new one, and the one that completes, archives or restores an item.

tags.name: GEO Writer
tags.description: AI-powered GEO Writer tasks (formerly Content Intelligence). Tasks are processed asynchronously, so create one and poll it until it completes. A finished article or update can be sent to the project's connected WordPress site as a draft, and that site's posts and pages can be read.

tags.name: Technical GEO Reports
tags.description: Run the technical GEO analysis bundle, then list, poll and retrieve each completed report.

tags.name: GEO Audits
tags.description: Audits re-run one technical GEO check type on a domain or URL, once or weekly/monthly. Each run is kept: compare runs check by check, follow issues across runs (new, fixed, regressed), accept known issues and read the alerts scheduled runs raised.

tags.name: Annotations
tags.description: Mark a date on the project timeline (a campaign launch, a site migration) so charts show what happened when.

tags.name: Team
tags.description: The account team: list members and pending invitations, invite someone by email with their projects and access, revoke an invitation or remove a member, with the same rules as the Team Members settings page. Not available to a key limited to some projects.

tags.name: API Keys
tags.description: The API keys of the user the calling key belongs to: list them, create a key limited to some of the account projects (for example one per customer project) and revoke one. Needs an account-wide read and write key; not available to a key limited to some projects.

tags.name: Store Integrations
tags.description: The endpoints behind the LLM Pulse app for Shopify: match a store to its project, push the orders AI assistants referred to the store and read them back, and turn catalog products into buyer prompts to track. They need an API key (Scale plan or above) and are not available to accounts with a white-label portal or an embed, which receive ERR_INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE (403).

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Outbound event notifications: subscribe an HTTPS URL to project events and receive HMAC-signed deliveries with no polling. Scale plan and above.

tags.name: MCP
tags.description: Model Context Protocol endpoint for AI clients (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other MCP-compatible assistants).

tags.name: OAuth 2.1
tags.description: OAuth 2.1 authorization for MCP clients: discovery metadata, dynamic client registration, authorization, token exchange and JWKS.

get.x-llms-description: Health check; validates the API key and optionally pings a project.
get.description: Validates the API key and optionally pings a project. Returns the authenticated user_id, project (if project_id is supplied), and a request_id. The project object carries only id, name and brand_name; GET /dimensions/projects/{id} returns the rest, pitch and tracked included.
get.x-rest-only: Key and project health check; an MCP client checks its connection with the initialize handshake.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Optional project to verify access for

get.summary: Account plan, quota usage and rate limits
get.x-llms-description: Plan, subscription window, quota usage (prompts, AI answers this tracking cycle, projects, competitors, intelligence tasks, pitch projects) and API rate limits for the authenticated account.
get.description: Returns the account plan, tracking cadence, subscription window, how much of each quota is used (prompts, projects, competitors per project, monthly GEO Writer tasks, team members, active recurring GEO audits, manual GEO audit runs in the last 24 hours, AI answers spent in the current tracking window with its reset time, and pitch projects created this month, with the account's pitch project access) and the published API rate limits. Limits resolve through the account owner, so a team member sees the capacity that applies to them. An unlimited quota returns limit and remaining as null with unlimited set to true, since Infinity is not representable in JSON. The subscription block is only present for callers who can access Billing and Plans in the app (the account owner, or a team member with billing access); everyone else gets the same response without that key. requests_per_minute is the ceiling of the key used for the call, not a fixed number. For a key limited to some projects, the response carries nothing about the rest of the account: plan, plan_name, subscription and limits.team_members are absent, api_key_project_ids lists the key's projects, limits.prompts.used counts those projects' prompts, limits.prompts, limits.intelligence_tasks, the two GEO audit quotas and limits.prompt_executions show only remaining and unlimited (the capacity the key can still spend, without the account total), limits.pitch_projects is absent, and the projects quota is capped at the projects it reaches. tracking_frequency stays, as the cadence those projects' data is collected at.

plan.description: Plan key (starter, growth, scale, ...). Absent for a key limited to some projects.

plan_name.description: Display name of the plan to show people (e.g. Scale++ for the scaleplusplus key). Absent for a key limited to some projects.

tracking_frequency.description: How often prompts run (weekly, daily, monthly, ...)

role.description: Whether the key belongs to the account owner or a team member

api_key_project_ids.description: The projects the calling API key is limited to; null for a key that sees the whole account, and for OAuth

subscription.description: Billing state. Present only for callers who can access Billing and Plans in the app; absent otherwise.

requests_per_minute.description: The ceiling enforced for the API key used on this call, which may be above the 300/min default.

write_requests_per_minute.description: Flat ceiling on write requests, the same for every key.

get.x-llms-description: List all projects accessible to the API key.
get.description: All projects accessible with your API key. Pitch projects, one-off snapshots deleted 90 days after they are created, are left out unless pitch is include or only.

parameters.name: pitch
parameters.description: exclude (default) leaves pitch projects out, include lists them with the tracked projects, only lists pitch projects alone

get.x-llms-description: Detailed info for one project: matching names, locale, industry, app store IDs, prompt limit, stats, data connection status.
get.description: Detailed info for one project: matching_names, additional_owned_domains, industry, business model, primary products, target audience, brand voice, locale, app store IDs, prompt_limit (the project's own prompt cap, null without one), project_type (the pricing agreement type the project is billed as, such as core or lean, null without one), stats (incl. prompts_by_brand_kind counts and prompts_available, how many prompts can still be added: the lower of the project's free slots and the account's remaining prompts, null when neither caps it), data_coverage (models, countries and languages with data), the status of each data connection (search_console, ai_traffic, agent_traffic) with the connect_url where the user connects it, and for a pitch project its pitch_expires_at and pitch_run (when it ran, the AI models it asked and how many answers arrived).

get.x-llms-description: List AI models the project has execution data for.
List countries and languages with data for the project.

post.x-llms-description: Start the multi-step project wizard: returns a draft_id + AI suggestions for the URL (name, description, industry, aliases).
post.description: Start the multi-step project-creation wizard. Returns a draft_id plus AI suggestions (name, description, industry, brand aliases) for the URL. Cold URLs can take up to ~2 minutes to analyze; pass suggest=false to skip AI and respond instantly. Drafts expire after 24h. Requires a `read_write` scope API key.

website_url.description: Public HTTP(S) URL with a DNS hostname or public IP address. Credentials, private and special IP addresses, localhost and internal hostnames are rejected.

201.description: Draft created; envelope with draft state, suggestions and limits

get.x-llms-description: Read a draft: state, current step, accumulated data; include_suggestions=true returns cached suggestions only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Draft id (draft_...)

parameters.name: include_suggestions
parameters.description: Cache-only: returns suggestions for the current step if already generated, never triggers AI

patch.x-llms-description: Submit a wizard step (details, prompts, competitors, owned_media) with strict forward gating; responds with next-step AI suggestions.
patch.description: Submit one step (details, prompts, competitors, owned_media). Strict forward gating: a step is only accepted when every previous step is complete (`ERR_DRAFT_STATE` otherwise); completed steps can be resubmitted. Responds with the updated draft plus AI suggestions for the next step.

brand_name.description: Defaults to name. Up to 100 characters, the name included when it stands in; finalize refuses a longer one with ERR_INVALID_PARAM

matching_names.description: Brand-name variants used to detect mentions (details step). At most 50 names of up to 100 characters each; the step stores the list as sent, and finalize refuses a longer list or name with ERR_INVALID_PARAM (422)

competitors.description: Competitors step: objects {domain, brand_name, matching_names}, capped by plan. Each competitor's matching_names takes at most 50 names of up to 100 characters, checked at finalize like POST /projects

post.summary: Finalize a draft into a real project
post.x-llms-description: Create the real project from a completed draft (idempotent; same effects as POST /projects).
post.description: Creates the project with all accumulated draft data (same effects as POST /projects). Idempotent: finalizing an already-finalized draft returns 200 with the existing project. Optional overrides: weekly_email_subscribed, execute_prompts_immediately.

post.x-llms-description: Create a complete project in one call (name, locale, prompts, competitors, owned media, Brand Book profile); idempotent via external_identifier.
post.description: Create a complete project in one call: project fields, prompts (queued for execution and categorization), collections tagging those prompts, competitors, weekly email subscription. With pitch true it creates a pitch project instead: a one-off snapshot for a prospect that runs once, takes no project slot and is deleted after 90 days unless converted; ERR_PLAN_REQUIRED when the account is below the Scale tier, on a trial or not an agency or platform account (error.meta.access says which), ERR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED when the month's pitch projects are used (error.meta.resets_on), ERR_INVALID_PARAM for more than 100 prompts or a domain the account tracks or pitched in the last 90 days. Accounts billed per project type under a pricing agreement choose the project's type with project_type (such as core or lean; omitted, the account's default type), which sets its prompt cap and its price. The response lists same_domain_projects so an accidental duplicate is visible; it never blocks the create. Its prompts get their first answers within about 24 hours, as far as the account's allowance of AI answers for the cycle covers them; the rest run when the allowance resets. Idempotent via `external_identifier` (embed-enabled accounts only; replay returns 200 with the existing project). Requires a `read_write` scope API key.

patch.x-llms-description: Update the project profile / Brand Book (brand_name, description, industry, business_model, target_audience, brand_voice, goals, primary_products, matching_names), additional_owned_domains (account owner only), prompt_limit and project_type (account owner or a co-owner with Projects update). A matching_names or additional_owned_domains change reprocesses past answers in the background.
patch.description: Updates the project name and profile, the same fields as Project Settings: name, brand_name, description, industry, business_model (plus business_model_other when it is OTHER), target_audience, brand_voice, goals, primary_products, matching_names, and the additional owned domains (additional_owned_domains). Send only the fields to change; unknown fields are rejected, and a request is applied whole or not at all. All seven Brand Book fields feed every GEO Writer task and prompt suggestions; only industry, description, and target_audience help Recommendations. A matching_names change re-runs mention/citation matching over the project history in the background, and an additional_owned_domains change reprocesses the past answers that cite an added or removed domain (rematching=true); further edits are rejected while that runs. Only the account owner can send additional_owned_domains: a team member key gets ERR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION and nothing is applied. prompt_limit sets or (null) removes the project's own prompt cap, as in Account Settings > Prompt Limits. Only the account owner or a co-owner whose permissions grant Projects update can send it (Account Settings > Prompt Limits lets any co-owner change it; here a co-owner, like every team member, also needs Projects update): any other team member gets ERR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION, and a key limited to some projects ERR_KEY_PROJECT_SCOPED, with nothing applied. A request that sends only prompt_limit is applied even while a rematch runs. project_type, for accounts billed per project type under a pricing agreement and sent on its own, moves the project to another of the account's types (such as core or lean): the new type's prompt cap applies at once and its price from the next renewal; it follows the prompt_limit rules on who may send it. pitch false, sent on its own, converts a pitch project into a tracked project, like Convert in the app: it keeps its answers and metrics, is no longer deleted, takes a project slot, and its prompts count against the prompt quota and run on the account's schedule from the next run. It cannot be undone and does not give back the month's pitch project. Converting needs the Projects update and create permissions (ERR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION) and a key for the whole account (ERR_KEY_PROJECT_SCOPED); ERR_LIMIT_REACHED, with error.meta.limit, when the account has no project slot or prompts left or the project has more prompts or competitors than the plan allows per project, and ERR_INVALID_PARAM when the project is not a live pitch project. A pitch project's website, brand name, matching names, country, language and prompt limit (and name while it has no brand name) are fixed from creation: changing one returns ERR_INVALID_PARAM, so convert it with pitch false first. Requires a `read_write` scope API key.

name.description: Project name shown in the app. A label: it does not change mention detection unless brand_name is empty. Cannot be blank

brand_name.description: Brand name used to detect mentions, up to 100 characters (a longer one is refused with ERR_INVALID_PARAM). Applies to future runs; it does not rewrite history

description.description: What the brand does. Context for Recommendations and GEO Writer (Brand Book)

industry.description: Single industry key (e.g. SAAS), stored as sent; an array of keys is also accepted and stored as an array, like the in-app multi-select. Unknown keys are rejected with the valid keys listed

business_model.description: Business model key (e.g. B2B_SAAS); unknown keys are rejected

business_model_other.description: Free-text business model, only accepted when business_model is OTHER; rejected against any other key

target_audience.description: Who the brand sells to (Brand Book)

brand_voice.description: Tone of voice guidance for generated content (Brand Book)

goals.description: What the brand wants to achieve. Context for GEO Writer and prompt suggestions

primary_products.description: Full replacement list of the main products or services

matching_names.description: FULL replacement list of the brand-name variants used to detect mentions; send every variant to keep. At most 50 names of up to 100 characters each; a longer list or name is refused with ERR_INVALID_PARAM (422) and nothing in the request is applied

additional_owned_domains.description: FULL replacement list (at most 10) of other domains the brand owns, such as a blog or a country site; [] clears it. Citations from them count as owned, like the project website. Each entry is a website's own domain and covers its subdomains; a pasted URL is stored as its domain (https://www.acme.co.uk/x becomes acme.co.uk). A list the domain editor would refuse (a subdomain such as blog.acme.com, a platform many companies share such as youtube.com, amazon.com or wordpress.com, the project website, a tracked competitor domain, a duplicate or an entry that is not a domain) is rejected with ERR_INVALID_PARAM and the reason. Order does not matter, and an unchanged list starts nothing. Account owner only, on every plan

prompt_limit.description: The most prompts this project can hold, a JSON integer from 1 to 2147483647; null removes the project's limit. A string, a decimal, 0 or a negative number is rejected with ERR_INVALID_PARAM. The account's plan allowance still applies, so the lower of the two wins (GET /dimensions/projects/{id} returns prompt_limit and stats.prompts_available). A limit below the current count keeps every prompt and refuses new ones until the project is under it; note says what the project can now hold. Account owner or a co-owner with Projects update permission only; a key limited to some projects answers ERR_KEY_PROJECT_SCOPED. The Swift, Kotlin, Dart and R clients leave a null field out of the request body, so they can set a limit but not remove one: remove it with a plain HTTP request that sends prompt_limit as null

project_type.description: Only for accounts billed per project type under a pricing agreement; any other account gets ERR_INVALID_PARAM. The key of one of the account's project types, such as core or lean. The new type's prompt cap applies at once and its price from the next renewal. Send it on its own: with other fields it answers ERR_INVALID_PARAM. Moving to a type whose cap is below the prompts the project holds answers ERR_INVALID_PARAM, and so do a pitch project and a project the team set up by hand (included at no cost, paused or with a raised prompt limit), which keeps its type; sending the type the project already has changes nothing. Account owner or a co-owner with Projects update permission only; a key limited to some projects answers ERR_KEY_PROJECT_SCOPED. It is applied even while a rematch runs

pitch.description: false converts a pitch project into a tracked project. Send it on its own, without other fields; true is rejected

403.description: A write with a read-only key answers ERR_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE. A team member whose permissions do not grant Projects update (a co-owner included), who sends additional_owned_domains, or who sends prompt_limit or project_type without being a co-owner answers ERR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION. A key limited to some projects that sends prompt_limit or project_type answers ERR_KEY_PROJECT_SCOPED. All with the same status, and nothing in the request is applied

delete.x-llms-description: Delete a whole project (irreversible; hidden at once, frees a project slot; its prompts, answers, mentions, citations, sentiment, competitors and metrics history are purged in the background).
delete.description: Deletes a project, like Delete Project in Project Settings, and cannot be undone. The project disappears at once from the app, GET /dimensions/projects and every other endpoint, and frees a project slot; a background job then deletes its prompts, answers, mentions, citations, sentiment, competitors and metrics history. API keys limited to it lose it, and a key left with no project is revoked. A project that is already being deleted, or that the key cannot see, answers ERR_PROJECT_NOT_FOUND. Requires an account-wide `read_write` scope API key: a key limited to some projects answers ERR_KEY_PROJECT_SCOPED. A team member needs permission to delete projects.

403.description: A read-only key answers ERR_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE and a key limited to some projects ERR_KEY_PROJECT_SCOPED: deleting a project acts on the whole account. A team member whose permissions do not grant deleting projects answers ERR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION. All with the same status, and nothing is deleted

get.x-llms-description: Time-series for one or more metrics, broken down by actor (brand + competitors).
get.description: Returns time-series data for one or more metrics, broken down by actor (project + competitors). Supports day/week/month granularity, with sticky carry-forward semantics for week/month aggregates.

get.x-llms-description: Aggregated period summary with totals (sum for counts; rates pooled over the window, as the app shows them; see aggregation field), min/max/last, plus position distribution.
get.description: Same as /metrics/timeseries but adds a `summary` block with total/min/max/last per metric per actor, plus a `position_distribution` block (Position 1, Position 2, Position 3+). Citations and citation rate include visible citations and background source references. Background references use position 0 and are excluded from avg_position and position distributions. `total` is a SUM for count metrics (mentions, citations, responses). For rate/percentage and average metrics (visibility/mention_rate, citation_rate, sentiment shares, net_sentiment, avg_position, avg_mention_position) it pools the whole window, the number the app shows for the same filters; visibility is all mentions over all responses, never a mean of the period rates, which would weigh a period of 2 responses like one of 200. ai_visibility_score is the window's points over its tracking runs. Rates are never summed. Each summary row carries an `aggregation` field (`sum` or `average`).

get.x-llms-description: Paginated per-prompt metrics (responses, mentions, citations, mention_rate, citation_rate, avg position, brand sentiment) with each prompt's country, language, type, brand focus and tags.
get.description: Paginated per-prompt aggregated metrics. Returns responses, mentions, citations, mention_rate, citation_rate, avg_mention_position and avg_position per prompt, plus the brand sentiment of its responses (sentiment_responses, the five sentiment percentages and net_sentiment, computed like the sentiment timeseries) and the prompt's classification (country_code, language_code, prompt_type, brand_kind and tags, as in /dimensions/prompts). Citations and citation rate include visible citations and background source references; avg_position uses visible citations only. Pass `breakdown=model` to split each prompt by model.

parameters.name: breakdown
parameters.description: Add per-(prompt, model) rows to the output

get.x-llms-description: Share of Voice for the project vs competitors (over time, current snapshot, Top-4 + Others breakdown).
get.description: Share of Voice breakdown comparing your project to competitors. Returns over_time, current snapshot, and a Top-4 + Others breakdown.

get.x-llms-description: Top cited domains across AI responses with sortable mention/citation stats.
get.description: Registrable domains most frequently cited in AI responses for the project, including visible citations and background source references. This endpoint remains a domain rollup when exact-subdomain matching is enabled. Results can be sorted by total responses, average mention rate, or average visibility.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Filter domains by case-insensitive partial match

parameters.name: collection_ids
parameters.description: Tags (collections) to include at once, as a union: one ID or a comma-separated list, e.g. collection_ids=12,15 (collection_ids[]=12&collection_ids[]=15 is also accepted). Combines with collection_id. An ID outside the project returns 422 ERR_INVALID_PARAM.

parameters.name: domains
parameters.description: Restrict the result to these exact domains, case-insensitive: one domain or a comma-separated list, e.g. domains=wikipedia.org,reddit.com. The bracket form domains[]=wikipedia.org&domains[]=reddit.com is also accepted.

get.x-llms-description: List competitors for a project (optionally including the project brand as actor_type=project).

parameters.name: include_project_brand
parameters.description: When true, prepends the project brand with actor_type=project and is_own=true

get.x-llms-description: Detailed info for one competitor: matching names, app store IDs, color.
The Competitors page's Suggested tab, competing brands the AI discovery proposed or the most cited domains not tracked yet.
get.description: The two lists of the Suggested tab of the Competitors page. `basis=brands` (default) returns the competing brands the AI discovery proposed that are not tracked or rejected yet, with the names it would match and, when counted, how many answers name it (`mentions`). `basis=citations` returns the domains AI answers cite most that are not your own or tracked yet, with how many answers cite each (`citations`). `discovery` tells whether a discovery run is still loading. Read-only: it never starts a discovery run, which the page starts from its Discover button. Add a suggestion with POST /competitors.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Only suggestions whose brand name or domain contains this text

post.x-llms-description: Add a competitor (brand_name + domain) to a project; respects the plan competitor cap.
post.description: Adds a competitor with its own citation URL matching rule. Honours the per-plan max competitors cap. A `domain` rule on the project's own domain, or one of its subdomains, or a `host` rule on the project's own host, returns ERR_INVALID_PARAM; a `path_prefix` rule on it is accepted. Requires a `read_write` scope API key.

domain.description: URL is accepted and normalised to host (e.g. https://www.openai.com → openai.com)

matching_names.description: Extra names this competitor is matched by; brand_name is added automatically. At most 50 names in all, brand_name included, of up to 100 characters each; a longer list or name is refused with ERR_INVALID_PARAM (422)

citation_match_mode.description: domain includes the registrable domain and all subdomains; host requires the exact hostname; path_prefix also requires citation_match_path

citation_match_path.description: Required when citation_match_mode=path_prefix, e.g. /es. Case-sensitive; trailing slash is optional; query and fragment are ignored

patch.x-llms-description: Update a competitor (brand_name, website domain or host, matching_names, color, citation rule). Name, website or rule changes re-run matching in the background.
patch.description: Updates brand_name, the competitor website domain or host, matching_names (full replacement list; the brand name is always included automatically), color and/or the citation URL matching rule. Website domain/host and citation-rule changes share one seven-day cooldown per competitor; other fields remain editable during the cooldown. Moving to a `domain` rule on the project's own domain, or a `host` rule on its own host, returns ERR_INVALID_PARAM. Name, website or citation-rule changes re-run historical matching in the background: the competitor shows processing=true for a few minutes and further edits are rejected meanwhile. Requires a `read_write` scope API key.

GscAggregationType.name: aggregation_type
GscAggregationType.description: How Google counts impressions. auto (default) is what Search Console shows (by page when page is grouped or filtered, else by property). Google rejects byProperty with a page dimension or filter.

GscStartRow.name: start_row
GscStartRow.description: Google ranks rows by clicks and returns at most 25,000 per request. start_row moves that window down the ranking (e.g. 25000 for the next block); sort and pagination apply within the window.

GscDataState.name: data_state
GscDataState.description: final (default) counts only rows Google has finalized. all also counts the most recent days, which are still being filled in and will change.

Range.name: range
Range.description: Number of days to look back (alternative to from/to, which win when both are given). A value that is not a plain positive number returns 422 ERR_INVALID_PARAM, even beside from/to.

To.name: to
To.description: End of the window. A date-only value such as 2026-09-01 covers that whole day. Pass a full timestamp to end the window earlier.

ListingFrom.name: from
ListingFrom.description: Start of the window. Sent alone, the window runs from it to the end of today. A from later than to, or a window longer than 1,500 days, returns 422 ERR_INVALID_PARAM.

ListingTo.name: to
ListingTo.description: End of the window. A date-only value such as 2026-09-01 covers that whole day. Pass a full timestamp to end the window earlier. Sent without from, the window covers the 30 days that end on it.

MetricsRange.name: range
MetricsRange.description: Number of days to look back, today included. Required unless from is given, and from/to win when both are given: a request with neither range nor from, or a range that is not a plain positive number (even beside from/to), returns 422 ERR_INVALID_PARAM.

MetricsFrom.name: from
MetricsFrom.description: Start of the window, instead of range (to then defaults to the end of today). Required unless range is given.

Model.name: model
Model.description: Filter by one AI model. It must be a model enabled for the API key's user: an unknown value, or a model the user has not enabled, returns 422 ERR_INVALID_PARAM with the valid values in the message.

MetricsModel.name: model
MetricsModel.description: Filter by one AI model. It must be a model enabled for the API key's user: an unknown value, or a model the user has not enabled, returns 422 ERR_INVALID_PARAM with the valid values in the message. The legacy values google-ai-mode and google-ai-overview are also accepted, as ai_mode and ai_overview.

CitationModel.name: model
CitationModel.description: Filter by one AI model. Only chatgpt, ai_overview, ai_mode, perplexity, gemini, naver_ai, baidu_ai, naver_ai_tab, qwen, doubao and bing_ai_mode are accepted: any other value, including another model enabled for the API key's user, returns 422 ERR_INVALID_PARAM (invalid model). One of those eleven that the user has not enabled also returns 422 ERR_INVALID_PARAM, with the valid values in the message.

CollectionId.name: collection_id
CollectionId.description: One collection/tag ID or a comma-separated list of IDs. A query value is always a string on the wire, so it is typed as one: the previous integer-or-string union made generators emit a wrapper type they could not serialize.

CountryCode.name: country_code
CountryCode.description: One ISO country code or a comma-separated list (e.g. US,GB,DE)

LanguageCode.name: language_code
LanguageCode.description: One ISO language code or a comma-separated list (e.g. en,es,de)

Prompt.name: prompt
Prompt.description: Filter by prompt ID. An id that is not a plain positive number, or that names no prompt of the project, returns 422 ERR_INVALID_PARAM.

PromptType.name: prompt_type
PromptType.description: One prompt type or a comma-separated list: informational, navigational, commercial, transactional

BrandKind.name: brand_kind
BrandKind.description: Filter by brand kind: brand (own brand/products), brand_other (competitors/other brands), non_brand (generic, no brand named). For fair 1:1 brand-vs-competitor comparisons (visibility, share of voice), use non_brand: brand-focused prompts skew results toward the brand they name. The in-app Overview page applies non_brand by default.

MentionFilter.name: mention_filter
MentionFilter.description: Filter by which brands are mentioned, as a two-axis matrix (your brand x competitors): mentions_you / not_mentions_you, mentions_competitor / not_mentions_competitor, and the four combined cells you_and_competitor, competitor_not_you (a rival wins and you are absent), you_not_competitor, no_brands (no tracked brand appears, i.e. open space; on answers, finished answers only). Combine with 'competitors' to narrow the competitor side to specific rivals; on a negative cell that reads 'none of these'. On /dimensions/sources it applies to the crawled content of each cited page instead of the answer text. The legacy value 'competitors_only' is still accepted as an alias of competitor_not_you.

CitationFilter.name: citation_filter
CitationFilter.description: Same two-axis matrix applied to the domains cited in the answer instead of the brands named in it (cites_no_brands still allows other domains), plus no_citations, finished answers that cite no source at all. Independent of mention_filter; pass both to intersect them (e.g. mentions_you + not_cites_you finds answers that talk about you without linking to you).

UrlSha256.name: url_sha256
UrlSha256.description: 64-character hex SHA-256 of the cited URL

PlanRequired.description: Endpoint requires a higher plan tier

GrowthPlanRequired.description: Endpoint requires the Growth plan or above

SearchConsoleForbidden.description: Plan below Growth (ERR_PLAN_REQUIRED), or Google revoked the project's Search Console access (ERR_SEARCH_CONSOLE_ACCESS_REVOKED): reconnect the property

error.message: Google Search Console access was revoked. Reconnect the property in Preferences > Project Settings > Connections.

KeyProjectScoped.description: Writes with a read-only key answer ERR_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, and a key limited to some projects ERR_KEY_PROJECT_SCOPED, with the same status: this operation acts on the whole account

InsufficientPermission.description: API key belongs to a team member whose permission matrix does not grant this feature

TeamForbidden.description: A key limited to some projects answers ERR_KEY_PROJECT_SCOPED, since the team belongs to the whole account. A team member without the Team Members permission, or asking for something only the owner or a co-owner can do, answers ERR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION, and a write with a read-only key ERR_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, with the same status

ApiKeysForbidden.description: A key limited to some projects answers ERR_KEY_PROJECT_SCOPED and a read-only key ERR_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE: managing keys needs an account-wide read and write key. A team member without the API Keys permission answers ERR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION, and creating a key below the Scale plan ERR_PLAN_REQUIRED, with the same status

IntegrationUnavailable.description: The account has a white-label portal or an embed, so store integrations are not available (ERR_INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE). Writes with a read-only key answer ERR_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, and a team member without the permission ERR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION, with the same status

error.message: Store integrations are not available for white-label or embed accounts

GenerationFailed.description: The AI generation failed; retry the request

error.message: suggestions could not be generated, try again

ServiceUnavailable.description: Upstream provider unavailable, retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header: Google's own value when it sent one, otherwise 900 after a quota error and 60 after an outage

error.message: Google Search Console is temporarily unavailable. Retry in a few minutes.

PortalWriteForbidden.description: Writes with a read-only key answer ERR_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, a team member without the permission ERR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION, and a request made on a white-label portal host, where the app does not offer this action, ERR_INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE, with the same status

ReportSendCooldown.description: The report was sent less than 10 minutes ago; retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header

error.message: This report was just sent; try again in 540 seconds

CmsForbidden.description: WordPress no longer accepts the stored application password, or its user cannot write posts (ERR_CMS_ACCESS_REVOKED, with error.meta.connect_url to reconnect). error.meta.reason says why: reconnect_required, authorization_header_lost (the password stopped reaching WordPress: revoked, or the server now strips the Authorization header), unknown_user, application_passwords_disabled, application_passwords_disabled_for_user, rest_api_restricted or missing_capability. A white-label portal host answers ERR_INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE, a read-only key on a write ERR_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE and a team member without the permission ERR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION, with the same status

error.message: WordPress no longer accepts the application password. Reconnect the site in Project Settings.

meta.message: WordPress no longer accepts the application password. Reconnect the site in Project Settings.

CmsNotConnected.description: The project has no WordPress connection (ERR_CMS_NOT_CONNECTED, with error.meta.connect_url), the project does not exist (ERR_PROJECT_NOT_FOUND), or the task or post does not (ERR_NOT_FOUND)

error.message: This project has no WordPress connection. Connect one in Project Settings.

meta.message: This project has no WordPress connection. Connect one in Project Settings.

CmsUnprocessable.description: A parameter failed validation (ERR_INVALID_PARAM), or WordPress refused the request, the site now redirects to another address or it can no longer be reached safely from our servers (ERR_CMS_REJECTED, error.meta.reason rejected, firewall_blocked, http_auth_required, invalid_json, redirected, unsafe_site, dns_failed or private_address; redirected carries error.meta.connect_url to reconnect). Retrying the same request gives the same answer

CmsUnavailable.description: The WordPress site could not be reached or took too long to answer (ERR_CMS_UPSTREAM). Retry later; error.meta.reason says why: unreachable, timeout, connection_refused, tls_error, server_error or maintenance

error.message: We could not reach the site. Try again later.

meta.message: We could not reach the site. Try again later.

SearchConsoleFilters.description: The value of the filters query parameter, JSON-encoded into a single string.

AccountQuota.description: A consumable quota. limit and remaining are null when unlimited is true. For a key limited to some projects, prompts and intelligence_tasks carry no limit (and intelligence_tasks no used): only the capacity left.

period.description: Reset window for quotas that reset (e.g. month)

AccountExecutionQuota.description: The account's allowance of AI answers for the current tracking window: its prompt limit times its enabled AI models, plus 5% so prompts can be replaced during the window. Every scheduled run and every first run of a new prompt spends one answer per AI model, and deleting a prompt gives nothing back. When it is used up, new prompts wait until resets_at. limit and remaining are null when unlimited is true. For a key limited to some projects, only remaining and unlimited (the account-wide answers left), period and resets_at.

period.description: The tracking window, from the account's tracking cadence (week runs Monday to Sunday)

resets_at.description: When the next window starts and the allowance is full again (00:00 Europe/Madrid)

AccountPitchQuota.description: Pitch projects created this calendar month (Europe/Madrid) against the monthly allowance, which pitch projects use instead of a project slot. limit and remaining are null when unlimited is true.

resets_on.description: The first day of next month, when the allowance starts again

access.description: Whether the account may create pitch projects, which are for agency and platform accounts (the account type, which the account owner or an account admin changes in Account Settings > Profile). none means the account is not an agency; approved access goes dormant while the account is below the Scale tier, on a trial, has a payment problem, is set to cancel or has an allowance of 0; revoked means our team turned it off. pending and rejected are no longer returned

AccountCapacity.description: A ceiling with no usage counter attached. limit is null when unlimited is true.

meta.description: Extra detail for some codes. A not-connected or access-revoked error from the Search Console, AI traffic, web analytics or agent traffic endpoints carries connect_url, the in-app page where the user connects or reconnects the source. A prompt write refused because a launched pitch project's prompts are fixed carries reason pitch_prompts_frozen.

brand_name.description: LLM-facing brand label (used in prompts and customer-facing charts). Null when not set, in which case prompts and charts use `name`.

tracked.description: Whether scheduled runs include this project. False when it is a pitch project, which runs once, when it is paused, or when the plan's project limit leaves it out (the oldest projects up to the limit run), so its prompts do not run

untracked_reason.description: Why tracked is false: pitch_project, paused or project_limit. Null when tracked

pitch.description: Whether this is a pitch project, a one-off snapshot that runs its prompts once, takes no project slot and is deleted at pitch_expires_at unless it is converted (PATCH /projects/{id} with pitch false)

pitch_expires_at.description: When a pitch project is deleted, with its data, unless it is converted first. Null for a tracked project

industry.description: Industry as stored: one key as a string (e.g. SAAS), or an array of key strings when the project was created with a list or the in-app multi-select. Deliberately untyped so generated clients decode either shape

business_model_other.description: Set only when business_model is OTHER

prompt_limit.description: The most prompts this project can hold, set by the account owner or a co-owner (Account Settings > Prompt Limits). Null when the project has no limit of its own; the account's plan allowance applies either way

project_type.description: The project type it is billed as under the account's pricing agreement, such as core or lean (its own, else the account's default type). Null for accounts without per-project types and for pitch projects

prompts_available.description: How many prompts can still be added to this project now, the same number the Prompts page offers. The lower of the project's free slots under prompt_limit and the account's remaining prompts; 0 when either is full (a project over its limit keeps its prompts). Null when neither caps it

pitch_run.description: The one run of a pitch project; null for a tracked project. Its answers are dated between launched_at and settled_at, so read its metrics with from set to the launched_at date (the default ranges leave out a pitch older than a few weeks)

status.description: starting before the run begins, running while answers arrive, ready once every AI model has answered or stopped trying

models.description: The AI models the run asks, fixed when it starts

data_coverage.description: AI models, countries and languages the project has data for

search_console.description: Google Search Console connection of the project, judged by its primary property. connected means the Search Console endpoints can answer; reconnect_required means Google refused the primary property's stored access, so reads without property return ERR_SEARCH_CONSOLE_ACCESS_REVOKED until it is reconnected at connect_url, while a property GET /search_console/properties lists as connected, or property=all, still answers; not_connected means the endpoints return ERR_SEARCH_CONSOLE_NOT_CONNECTED.

property.description: The primary property (e.g. sc-domain:example.com), null when not connected

connect_url.description: The in-app page where the property is connected or reconnected (Preferences > Project Settings > Connections)

properties_count.description: Connected properties Google still accepts (reconnect_required ones excluded); GET /search_console/properties lists every property with its status

ai_traffic.description: Web analytics provider behind /metrics/ai_traffic and /web_analytics. connected means both answer; reconnect_required means the provider refused the stored access, so /metrics/ai_traffic still answers from synced data and /web_analytics returns ERR_WEB_ANALYTICS_ACCESS_REVOKED until it is reconnected at connect_url; not_connected means they return ERR_AI_TRAFFIC_NOT_CONNECTED and ERR_WEB_ANALYTICS_NOT_CONNECTED.

provider.description: The connected provider (e.g. google_analytics, adobe_analytics, adobe_cja, posthog, plausible, matomo, piano), null when not connected

connect_url.description: The in-app AI Traffic page, where the provider is connected or reconnected

agent_traffic.description: Agent traffic source behind /metrics/agent_traffic. connected and reconnect_required (the source refused the stored access, so syncing stopped) both answer from stored data; imported means no live source is connected but imported logs answer; not_connected means it returns ERR_AGENT_TRAFFIC_NOT_CONNECTED.

provider.description: The connected source (e.g. cloudflare_graphql, bunny_cdn, s3 or the log drain's provider), null without a live source

connect_url.description: The in-app Agent Analytics page, where a source is connected or reconnected

AdditionalOwnedDomains.description: Other domains the brand owns (at most 10, each a website's own domain covering its subdomains), whose citations count as owned like the project website. Empty when none

ProjectProfile.description: The project name and profile, as PATCH /projects/{id} and the update_project MCP tool return them

industry.description: Industry as stored: one key as a string (e.g. SAAS), or an array of key strings. Deliberately untyped so generated clients decode either shape

business_model_other.description: Set only when business_model is OTHER

prompt_limit.description: The most prompts this project can hold, set by the account owner or a co-owner (Account Settings > Prompt Limits). Null when the project has no limit of its own; the account's plan allowance applies either way

project_type.description: The project type it is billed as under the account's pricing agreement, such as core or lean. Null for accounts without per-project types and for pitch projects

rematching.description: True when a matching_names or additional_owned_domains change started a background recalculation of past answers; further edits are rejected until it finishes

note.description: What the change does to mention detection, citation ownership and historical numbers, and, when prompt_limit was sent, how many prompts the project holds and how many more can be added; after pitch false, what the converted project now uses
What happens next; the deletion cannot be undone

domain.description: Bare (scheme-less) domain. Null only on the own-brand row (include_project_brand=true) when the project has no URL.

matching_names.description: Alternative names matched as this competitor. Absent on the own-brand row

citation_match_path.description: Set only when citation_match_mode is path_prefix
Set only when citation_match_mode is path_prefix

google_play_name.description: English app name on Google Play, when the competitor has an Android app

app_store_name.description: English app name on the App Store, when the competitor has an iOS app

processing.description: True while the competitor's historical mentions are being recalculated

CitationMatchMode.description: How citations are attributed: domain (the domain and its subdomains), host (that exact host) or path_prefix (URLs under citation_match_path)

domain.description: Bare (scheme-less) domain. Null for the project actor when the project has no URL.

date.description: Calendar day in Europe/Madrid (YYYY-MM-DD). With granularity week or month it is the first day of the bucket (the Monday, or the 1st of the month).

value.description: Null when the metric has no value for the bucket, e.g. a rate, position or sentiment metric on a day without answers.

total.description: Count metrics sum the buckets. Rate, position and sentiment metrics pool the whole window, the number the app shows for the same filters, whatever the granularity; visibility is all mentions over all responses x 100, citation_rate all citations over all responses x 100, a sentiment share all verdicts of that kind over all verdicts x 100, an average position the average of every position recorded in the window. They are never a mean of the bucket values. ai_visibility_score (weighted_visibility) is the window's points divided by its tracking runs (the days, weeks or months at the account's tracking frequency with responses under the filters).

aggregation.description: How total combines the buckets. sum for counts; average for rates, positions and sentiment, pooled over the window, and for ai_visibility_score, a per-run score

app_url.description: Opens this prompt in the app. The link names its project, so it opens there for any user with access to that project

country_code.description: Country of the prompt, as in /dimensions/prompts

language_code.description: Language of the prompt, as in /dimensions/prompts

prompt_type.description: Search intent: informational, navigational, commercial or transactional. Null until the prompt is classified

brand_kind.description: Brand focus: brand, brand_other or non_brand. Null until the prompt is classified

tags.description: Every tag the prompt belongs to

sentiment_responses.description: Responses in the window with a sentiment verdict for the brand, the base of the sentiment percentages (deduplicated like the sentiment timeseries)

sentiment_very_positive.description: Percentage (0-100) of sentiment_responses whose brand verdict is very positive; null when sentiment_responses is 0

sentiment_positive.description: Percentage (0-100) of sentiment_responses whose brand verdict is positive; null when sentiment_responses is 0

sentiment_neutral.description: Percentage (0-100) of sentiment_responses whose brand verdict is neutral; null when sentiment_responses is 0

sentiment_negative.description: Percentage (0-100) of sentiment_responses whose brand verdict is negative; null when sentiment_responses is 0

sentiment_very_negative.description: Percentage (0-100) of sentiment_responses whose brand verdict is very negative; null when sentiment_responses is 0

net_sentiment.description: Positive minus negative percentages (-100 to 100), neutral counted in the base; null when sentiment_responses is 0

periods.description: Per-bucket sample size and completeness: mentions is the total the shares were computed on (1-3 mentions produce the 100/50/33.33 low-sample patterns); partial marks buckets still collecting data or clipped by the requested window; confidence and margin_of_error read the sample size.

confidence.description: How far the shares of this period can be trusted, from its mentions: none (0), low (under 30), medium (under 100) or high (100 or more).

margin_of_error.description: Worst-case 95% margin of a share in percentage points, 98 / sqrt(mentions); mentions within one answer are not independent, so the real margin is at least this wide. null with no mentions.

sample.description: The period the current shares were computed on (the last one with mentions), same shape as a periods item; null when the window has no mentions.

previous_share.description: The actor's share in the last complete bucket before the current one; null without complete history.

avg_share.description: Mean share across complete buckets with data (partial buckets excluded); null without complete history.

others.description: Actors ranked fifth and below, folded into the Others share of breakdown

MetricsFiltersEcho.description: The filters the response was computed with, as the server resolved them. Each endpoint echoes only the keys it reads; a filter that was not given comes back null (or an empty list).

metrics.description: Requested metrics after alias resolution (mention_rate is echoed as visibility)

model.description: The model filter, or null when absent or not enabled for the account

collection_id.description: The collection_id parameter as sent (one id or a comma-separated list)

competitors.description: Competitor ids from the competitors parameter; empty when it was not given

query.description: Only present when a query filter was given

AiModelInsightsSummaryResponse.description: One entry per AI model the account has enabled or that answered in the window, in the in-app column order: the models list, which every per-model list and map in summary follows. A share, net sentiment or market share value with nothing behind it is null, because 0 is a real value; counts, totals and weighted visibility scores stay 0.

models.description: The AI models the account has enabled or that answered in the window, in the in-app column order

total_citations.description: Citations of the brand's URLs across the models

total_sentiments.description: Brand sentiment verdicts across the models

total_weighted_visibility_score.description: The brand's AI Visibility Score across the enabled models, its points there divided by the tracking runs with answers in any of them (the Overview's number for the same filters; a model that answered while disabled keeps its row but stays out of it); 0 when it has none

actors.description: The project and each competitor with a sentiment verdict in the window (only the competitors given in competitors, when it is given), by total_sentiments descending
The project and each competitor with an AI Visibility Score in the window, 0 included (only the competitors given in competitors, when it is given), by total_weighted_visibility_score descending

AiModelInsightsFiltersEcho.description: The filters the summary was computed with, as the server resolved them. A filter that was not given is left out, except granularity and competitors.

granularity.description: day, week or month; day when not given

competitors.description: Competitor ids from the competitors parameter; empty when it was not given

model.description: AI model key, as /dimensions/models lists it

color.description: Hex color the app charts the model with

mentions_count.description: Brand mentions in the model's answers; 0 when it has none

share_of_total.description: The model's percentage (0-100) of total_mentions; null when total_mentions is 0

citations_count.description: Citations of the brand's URLs in the model's answers; 0 when it has none

share_of_total.description: The model's percentage (0-100) of total_citations; null when total_citations is 0

sentiments_count.description: Brand sentiment verdicts in the model's answers

net_sentiment.description: positive_count minus negative_count as a percentage (-100 to 100) of sentiments_count, neutral verdicts counted in the base; null when sentiments_count is 0

weighted_visibility_score.description: The brand's AI Visibility Score in the model, its points there divided by the days the model answered; 0 when it has none

share_of_total.description: The model's percentage (0-100) of the brand's AI Visibility Score points; null when the brand has none

AiModelRateMatrix.description: Each actor's rate within each model: mentions of the actor (mentions_market_share), or answers citing it (citations_market_share), per answer of the model. Rates are independent, so the actors of a model can add up to more or less than 100.

denominators_by_model.description: Answers of each model in the window, keyed by model

actors.description: The project and each competitor with a mention (or citation) in the window (only the competitors given in competitors, when it is given), by total descending

AiModelRateMatrixActor.description: An actor (the standard actor shape) with one rate cell per model

competitor_id.description: Null for the project, the competitor id otherwise

domain.description: Bare (scheme-less) domain. Null for the project actor when the project has no URL.

total.description: The actor's numerators summed over the models

models.description: One cell per model, keyed by model

value.description: numerator as a percentage (0-100) of denominator; null when the model has no answers in the window

numerator.description: Mentions of the actor (or answers citing it) in the model's answers

denominator.description: Answers of the model in the window

AiModelSentimentMatrixActor.description: An actor (the standard actor shape) with one net sentiment cell per model

competitor_id.description: Null for the project, the competitor id otherwise

domain.description: Bare (scheme-less) domain. Null for the project actor when the project has no URL.

total_sentiments.description: The actor's sentiment verdicts summed over the models

models.description: One cell per model, keyed by model

value.description: The actor's net sentiment in the model, positive_count minus negative_count as a percentage (-100 to 100) of total_sentiments; null when total_sentiments is 0

total_sentiments.description: The actor's sentiment verdicts in the model's answers

AiModelWeightedVisibilityMatrixActor.description: An actor (the standard actor shape) with one AI Visibility Score cell per model

competitor_id.description: Null for the project, the competitor id otherwise

domain.description: Bare (scheme-less) domain. Null for the project actor when the project has no URL.

total_weighted_visibility_score.description: The actor's AI Visibility Score across the enabled models, its points there divided by the project's tracking runs with answers in them, so actors compare

models.description: One cell per model, keyed by model

value.description: The actor's AI Visibility Score in the model, its points there divided by the project's tracking runs with answers in that model; 0 when it has none

property.description: The property, site, report suite (rsid:...), data view (dataview:...) or project every query runs on.

query_language.description: The native query format the provider accepts.

docs_url.description: The provider's reference for that format.

allowed_fields.description: Top-level query fields that are forwarded.

rules.description: What the bridge enforces and the provider's main constraints.

fields.description: The provider's live field list where it offers one: GA4 dimensions and metrics with custom definitions, Adobe ids, Matomo report methods, PostHog event names, the Plausible catalog. Null when the provider did not return it.

fields_unavailable.description: Present when the field list could not be read; the format and example still apply.

kind.description: dimension or metric, when the provider says.

type.description: The provider's column type, when it says (PostHog).

label.description: The provider's display label, when it sends one (Piano).

rows.description: One array per row, values in column order: strings, numbers or null.

total_rows.description: Rows the provider has for the query, when it reports it.

truncated.description: True when the provider has more rows than returned; page with its own offset or page field.

totals.description: Metric totals by metric name, when the query asked for them.

notes.description: Provider caveats: sampling, thresholds, more rows available.

meta.description: Provider metadata such as GA4 time zone, currency and remaining property quota.

cached.description: True when the answer came from the 10-minute cache instead of the provider.

query.description: The request as sent to the provider, with the connected property forced and limits applied.

response.description: The AI answer. For a declined answer (no_result_reason declined) it is the reply the model gave instead; for no_answer it is a placeholder, not an AI response

duration_ms.description: Milliseconds, rounded to one decimal place

success.description: Null while the answer is still pending

no_result.description: True for a sentinel non-answer (no answer could be collected after all retries, or the model declined to answer, today only Gemini); excluded from platform metrics

no_result_reason.description: Present only when no_result is true. declined = the model declined to answer (today only Gemini, shown as Declined in the app) and response holds its reply; no_answer = no answer could be collected

sentiments.description: Needs the Growth plan or above; left out below it and named in plan_required_fields

shopping_products.description: Needs the Scale plan or above; left out below it and named in plan_required_fields
